Joe Armstrong (1950-2019) was a Swedish computer
scientist best known as the principal creator of Erlang, a programming language
designed for highly concurrent, fault-tolerant systems.
Joe Armstrong (1950-2019) was a Swedish computer
scientist best known as the principal creator of Erlang, a programming language
designed for highly concurrent, fault-tolerant systems.
He developed Erlang at Ericsson in the 1980s, along with Mike Williams and
Robert Virding. Its ideas, including lightweight processes, message passing,
supervision, and "let it crash" error handling, strongly influenced modern
distributed systems and frameworks such as Elixir and Phoenix.
Joe Armstrong (1950-2019) was a Swedish computer

Armstrong also co-authored Concurrent Programming in Erlang and earned a PhD
